construct: A large iodide load acutely suppresses thyroid hormone synthesis (Wolff-Chaikoff effect). After several days, normal thyroid tissue escapes by decreasing sodium-iodide symporter expression/activity, lowering intrathyroidal iodide below the inhibitory threshold and allowing organification and hormone synthesis to resume.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A large iodide load initially suppresses organification; normal thyroid tissue escapes after several days by reducing NIS-mediated iodide uptake and lowering intrathyroidal iodide below the inhibitory threshold.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Pendrin participates in apical iodide movement and TPO in organification, but the established escape mechanism is decreased basolateral NIS expression/activity.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Continued plasma iodide with recovery of synthesis specifically requires reduced thyroidal iodide entry via NIS.
